config.title: Props Drilling

intro.title: Props Drilling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application with TypeScript to understand props drilling. You will create a component hierarchy where data is passed down from a parent component to deeply nested child components through props. The core concept you'll learn is how to manage and pass data between components without using state management libraries, which is a fundamental React pattern. You'll work with functional components, TypeScript interfaces for type-safe props, and the JSX syntax for rendering. By the end, you'll see how props drilling works in practice and recognize its use cases and limitations.
intro.usecase: Props drilling is a common pattern in React applications where data needs to flow through multiple intermediate components to reach deeply nested child components. You'll encounter this when building complex UI structures like e-commerce product pages where user selections (size, color) must pass from the main product component down to cart buttons, or in dashboard applications where user preferences cascade from settings panels to individual chart widgets. This pattern appears in form-heavy applications where validation state or input values need to reach nested field components, and in content management systems where editing controls pass through layout wrappers to reach specific content blocks. Understanding props drilling helps you manage data flow in real-world component hierarchies before exploring more advanced state management solutions.

objectives: Define a functional component in TypeScript to serve as the root of a component hierarchy.
Implement a TypeScript interface to specify the shape of props passed to a component.
Assign props to a child component by passing them as attributes in JSX.
Access props within a child component to render dynamic content.
Construct a component tree by nesting multiple components that pass data down.
Utilize the spread operator to pass all props from a parent to a child component.
Apply destructuring assignment to extract specific props within a component's parameter list.
Handle optional props by defining them with a union type or optional modifier in the interface.
Modify a prop's value at an intermediate component before passing it further down the tree.
Return JSX elements that correctly display data received through props at each level.
Compare the prop values at different levels of the component tree to verify data flow.
Control the data flow by ensuring props are passed correctly through each intermediate component.

steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: The code includes an import statement that imports React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState from 'react'. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for state management.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there's something missing. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look quite right. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named 'App' that returns null for now. Use TypeScript syntax and define it after the imports.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. Make sure to specify the return type as JSX.Element or let TypeScript infer it.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an App component defined that returns null. This will be the main component for your props drilling example.
successCriteria: Component named 'App' is defined
Component returns null
Component uses TypeScript syntax (function or arrow with proper typing)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component. This component will serve as the entry point for our props drilling demonstration.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you name the component 'App'? Does it return null? Make sure to use TypeScript syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a functional component called 'App' that returns null. Remember to use TypeScript syntax.

steps.title: Create a UserProfile component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named UserProfile. For now, define it to take no props and return an empty div element.
steps.hint: You can create a functional component using either the function keyword or an arrow function. Make sure to export it so it can be used in other components.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a new UserProfile component that returns an empty div element.
successCriteria: The code includes a functional component named UserProfile that returns JSX (an empty div).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the UserProfile component. This component will later receive props to demonstrate props drilling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a functional component named UserProfile that returns JSX (like an empty div).
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserProfile component wasn't created correctly. Please create a functional component named UserProfile that returns an empty div element.

steps.title: Create a UserDetails component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named UserDetails that returns an empty <div> element. This component will later receive props through drilling.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called UserDetails that returns JSX. For now, just return a simple <div>.
steps.expectedOutcome: A UserDetails component is created and ready to be used as a child component.
successCriteria: The code contains a functional component named UserDetails that returns a JSX element (like <div>).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the UserDetails component. This component will serve as a deeper child in our props drilling example.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a component named UserDetails that returns JSX (like <div>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserDetails component isn't properly defined. Create a function or arrow function named UserDetails that returns JSX.

steps.title: Define props interface for UserProfile
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'UserProfileProps' for the UserProfile component. The interface should define a single property 'userName' of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the property with its type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TypeScript interface named UserProfileProps with a userName property of type string is created.
successCriteria: interface
UserProfileProps
userName
string
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the UserProfileProps interface with the correct property type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your interface includes all required elements: interface name 'UserProfileProps' and a 'userName' property of type string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface wasn't created correctly. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword, name it 'UserProfileProps', and include a 'userName: string' property.

steps.title: Define props interface for UserDetails
steps.instruction: Create an interface named UserDetailsProps for the UserDetails component's props. It should have a single property: userName of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword to define the props type. Place it above the UserDetails component.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a UserDetailsProps interface ready to use for typing the UserDetails component's props.
successCriteria: The interface should be named UserDetailsProps and contain a userName property of type string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the UserDetailsProps interface with the correct property type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the interface is named UserDetailsProps and has a userName property of type string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface is missing or incorrect. Please create an interface named UserDetailsProps with a userName: string property.

steps.title: Initialize user state in App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'userName' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the type parameter <string> since TypeScript needs to know the state type.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing state with useState
const [userName, setUserName] = useState<string>('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a userName state variable initialized to an empty string, ready to be passed down to child components.
successCriteria: App component contains useState call
State variable named 'userName'
Initial value is empty string
Type parameter <string> is used
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the userName state in the App component. This state will serve as the source of data that we'll pass down through the component tree.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you name the state variable 'userName'? Did you provide the initial value as an empty string? Did you include the TypeScript type parameter <string>?
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the App component, use useState to create a state variable. The syntax should look like: const [userName, setUserName] = useState<string>('');

steps.title: Pass userName prop to UserProfile
steps.instruction: In the App component's return statement, render the UserProfile component and pass the userName state value as a prop.
steps.hint: You need to use JSX syntax to render the component and pass the prop. The prop name should match what you defined in the UserProfileProps interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserProfile component should be rendered inside App with the userName prop passed from App's state.
successCriteria: UserProfile component is rendered in App's return statement with the userName prop correctly passed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the UserProfile component and passed the userName prop from App's state. This demonstrates how props flow from parent to child component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there might be an issue with how you're passing the prop. Make sure you're using the correct prop name and passing the userName state value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserProfile component isn't being rendered with the userName prop. Check that you're rendering <UserProfile /> in App's return statement and passing userName={userName} as a prop.

steps.title: Receive and display userName in UserProfile
steps.instruction: Update the UserProfile component to accept the UserProfileProps interface and display the userName prop in its JSX.
steps.hint: Add the props parameter to UserProfile with the correct type, then use the userName value inside the returned JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserProfile component now receives the userName prop and displays it in the UI.
successCriteria: UserProfile should accept a prop of type UserProfileProps and render the userName value inside its JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully updated UserProfile to receive and display the userName prop.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure UserProfile accepts the UserProfileProps interface and uses the userName prop in the JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserProfile component still needs to accept the userName prop and display it.

steps.title: Pass userName prop from UserProfile to UserDetails
steps.instruction: Inside the UserProfile component, render the UserDetails component and pass the userName prop that UserProfile receives to UserDetails.
steps.hint: You need to use the UserDetails component inside UserProfile's return statement and pass the userName prop through.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserProfile component will render UserDetails and pass the userName prop through, demonstrating props drilling through an intermediate component.
successCriteria: UserDetails component is rendered inside UserProfile
userName prop is passed from UserProfile to UserDetails
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully passed the userName prop from UserProfile to UserDetails, demonstrating props drilling through an intermediate component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're both rendering UserDetails inside UserProfile AND passing the userName prop to it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the UserProfile component, you need to render the UserDetails component and pass the userName prop to it.

steps.title: Receive and display userName in UserDetails
steps.instruction: Update the UserDetails component to receive the userName prop from its props interface and display it in the component's markup.
steps.hint: Add the userName parameter to UserDetails function with the correct type annotation, then use it inside the returned JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserDetails component should now properly receive the userName prop and display it in the UI, completing the props drilling chain.
successCriteria: UserDetails function receives userName parameter
Parameter is typed with UserDetailsProps interface
userName is displayed in JSX using curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully updated UserDetails to receive and display the userName prop. This completes the props drilling chain from App → UserProfile → UserDetails.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure UserDetails receives the userName parameter with the correct type annotation (UserDetailsProps) and displays it in the JSX using curly braces like {userName}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserDetails component needs to be updated to receive the userName prop. Add the parameter with type annotation and display it in the returned JSX.

steps.title: Add input to update userName in App
steps.instruction: In the App component's return statement, add an input field with its value bound to the userName state and an onChange handler that updates userName using setUserName.
steps.hint: Use an <input> element with value={userName} and onChange={(e) => setUserName(e.target.value)}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have an input field that allows the user to type and update the userName state, which will then propagate through props drilling to UserProfile and UserDetails.
successCriteria: The input element must have value={userName} and onChange={(e) => setUserName(e.target.value)} attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added an input field that updates the userName state. Now when you type in the input, the userName state changes and the new value will be passed down through props to UserProfile and UserDetails, demonstrating props drilling in action.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input field, but it's missing either the value binding to userName or the onChange handler to update the state. Make sure to include both value={userName} and onChange={(e) => setUserName(e.target.value)}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field is not properly implemented. You need to add an <input> element with value bound to userName state and an onChange handler that calls setUserName with the new value from e.target.value.
